_tooltips.id: Unique within your organization, e.g. OrderCreatedEvent. Workflows and other features refer to the event by it, so avoid changing it later.
_tooltips.name: The event's name as people see it in pickers and lists, e.g. Order created.
_tooltips.description: A note on when the event happens and what it is used for; users do not see it.
_tooltips.kind: SYSTEM: raised by the platform when a record changes. MESSAGE: sent to one receiver through the API. SIGNAL: broadcast to every listener through the API.
_tooltips.subjectType: For SYSTEM events only: the code of the entity type whose records raise the event, e.g. order.
_tooltips.action: For SYSTEM events only: what happens to the record: CREATED, UPDATED, DELETED, STATE_CHANGED or SIGNED (a document was signed for it).
_tooltips.state: For STATE_CHANGED only: the state the record enters, e.g. CONFIRMED.
_tooltips.releaseState: Whether the running application uses this definition as it stands: NEW was never published, CHANGED differs from what was published, RELEASED is what the application uses. Publish in the Release section to change it. Set by the system.
_tooltips.parameters: The values every occurrence of the event carries, e.g. an order and its order number. Workflows read them by name.

_tooltips.name: Unique within the event; letters, digits and _. For a SYSTEM event it must be an attribute of the subject — pick one of the suggestions, e.g. orderNumber — because that attribute's value fills it. The record itself is always carried as subject, which is reserved, so it needs no parameter.
_tooltips.type: The kind of value: STRING, NUMBER, BOOLEAN, DATE, or ENTITY_REF for a reference to a record.
_tooltips.entityType: For ENTITY_REF only: the type of record the parameter points at, e.g. order, or document. Not the attribute a SYSTEM parameter is filled from — that is its name.
_tooltips.required: Whether every occurrence of the event has to carry a value for this parameter.
_tooltips.description: A note on what the value means; users do not see it.
